citations.claim: after 1 step almost touching wall, distance ~0.022

counterfactual.change: Reduced vx from -49.99 to -9.99 and vy from -17.47 to -3.47 (speed ~10.5 m/s) keeping dt, wall, steps same; tunneling disappears because per-substep travel no longer skips the thin wall collision.

explanation: Body moves at ~53 m/s toward a thin horizontal wall (h=0.2). In step 0 distance_to_surface=0.56, step1 almost touching 0.023 with 22 substeps, but step2 penetrates -0.228 (>0.15 limit) because the collision with the thin edge/corner is missed under large dt (0.012) despite substepping. Substep displacement ~0.028m is small but the swept test vs AABB corner fails for grazing high-speed approach, allowing tunneling through the top edge area and then deep penetration. Reducing speed or dt removes violation.
vision_note: The red body starts just above and to the right of the thin horizontal wall's right tip. In step 1 it touches the corner, and in step 2 it is visibly intersecting and sinking into the end of the wall.
